A high-side reverse-polarity/series switch requires a P-channel FET; an N-channel FET with its gate referenced to ground cannot turn on when the source sits at +24 V.

Actually the spec component table: T2 — IRLR2905 main circulation pump; T3 — AON6407 ATO solenoid valve. But in the schematic image 1, the reverse polarity protection MOSFET is labeled "T3 AON6407". And in image 3 (the bottom part of page 1, ATO valve section), the MOSFET is labeled T5 A03400A. Hmm.

Wait, this is a discrepancy between spec's narrative mapping and schematic. But the spec says "T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch | Netlist: drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904)."

The instructions say the spec describes intended design; where it's silent judge with standard practice. The spec explicitly states T3 = AON6407 = ATO valve switch. But the schematic uses AON6407 (T3) as reverse polarity protection and A03400A (T5) as ATO valve switch.

Actually wait. Let me look at the AON6407 symbol in power train. The symbol there: it's drawn as a P-channel MOSFET? The arrow on source points... Let me look. The circle symbol with gate on bottom (Source label at bottom), the body diode orientation. Hard to tell. AON6407 is actually an N-channel MOSFET (per spec "8-DFN N-MOSFET"). For reverse polarity protection high-side, you'd typically use a P-channel MOSFET with source at input, gate pulled to ground via zener. If they used an N-channel AON6407 as high-side reverse polarity protection, that's wrong because the source would be at the load side and gate drive wouldn't work. Hmm.

Let's look at the symbol orientation in image 1 power train. The MOSFET symbol: left terminal connects to +24V (after F1), labeled with a wire going to the right to "+24V" rail (the big rail with C6 etc). Hmm, that's odd for reverse polarity.

Actually for a high-side P-MOSFET reverse polarity protection: source = input (V_in), drain = output (V_load), gate = pulled to ground (or to source via resistor) so that when V_in correct, V_gs = -V_in turns it on. The zener D3 12V protects gate-source. R7 33k is gate-source resistor. In the schematic, the gate would connect to R7 and D3. The source connects to input.
